study_info.title: Effects of Weight-Bearing Biofeedback Training on Functional Movement Patterns Following Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Randomized Controlled Trial
study_info.authors: Cory L. Christiansen, PT, PhD; Michael J. Bade, PT, PhD; Bradley S. Davidson, PhD; Michael R. Dayton, MD; Jennifer E. Stevens-Lapsley, PT, PhD
study_info.journal: Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy
study_info.study_design: Randomized controlled trial with concealed allocation using block randomization (block sizes of 4) and stratification on sex; randomization was carried out with a random number generator and occurred at the time of discharge from acute hospitalization to home; evaluators were blinded.
study_info.inclusion_criteria: Patients with knee osteoarthritis (OA), scheduled to undergo unilateral total knee arthroplasty (TKA).
study_info.exclusion_criteria: Neurological, vascular, or cardiac problems that limited function; contralateral knee pain (pain with activity greater than 2/10 on a numerical rating scale); other orthopedic conditions in the lower extremities that limited function; body mass index greater than 40 kg/m²; uncontrolled diabetes; smoking or drug abuse; living greater than 45 minutes away from the outpatient rehabilitation clinic; admission to a sub-acute inpatient rehabilitation facility; a surgical complication necessitating an altered course of rehabilitation; unable to walk 30 meters without an assistive device; unable to rise from a chair without arm use.
study_info.study_setting: Two local hospital systems in Colorado, United States; acute care, home-health, and outpatient physical therapy settings.
study_info.source_of_recruitment: Patients scheduled for unilateral TKA were recruited from two local hospital systems with a total of 9 participating orthopedic surgeons.
study_info.dropout_reasons: One patient in the RELOAD group dropped out due to time constraints and one patient in the CONTROL group dropped out due to transportation difficulties during the intervention. One additional patient from each group dropped out between the 6 and the 26-week time point: one due to a late infection and one due to moving.

minimal_units.intervention_details: Standard of care rehabilitation plus weight-bearing biofeedback training using a Nintendo Wii Fit Plus game and Wii Balance Board, with progressive games and exercises including static and dynamic bilateral stance, sit to stand, unilateral stance, and lunging, performed under therapist supervision and as a home exercise program.
minimal_units.intervention_frequency: Twice weekly supervised sessions plus daily home exercise program
minimal_units.adherence_to_intervention: The RELOAD group performed the standard of care HEP 1.0 ± 0.3 and the Wii HEP 0.8 ± 0.2 sessions per day. The total time spent for the RELOAD group with the Wii HEP was 14.2 ± 5.2 minutes per day, for a total time of 538 ± 199 minutes over the 6-week intervention.
